prize_parts.citation: For the development of ligand-controlled palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I keep B046 with Buchwald and Hartwig as my final position. The scientific case is unchanged by round 1: bulky, electron-rich phosphine and carbene ligands control oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination, and that control turned a narrow, harsh aryl amination into a general catalytic reaction. After about three decades the mechanism is independently confirmed and the reaction is used daily at scale in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. Credit is the cleanest on the shortlist: two investigators built complementary general ligand families in parallel and each developed the mechanistic picture. On the chair's question about the 2010 prize, the sentence I would defend is that the 2010 prize recognised carbon-carbon bond formation through transmetalation, whereas this prize recognises catalytic construction of carbon-nitrogen bonds, where amine binding and a harder reductive elimination required new ligand design, so the citation should say ligand-controlled C-N coupling. On the Kosugi, Migita, Guram and Rennels question, excluding them is defensible on generality: the earlier tin-amide and early amination reports were narrow or stoichiometric in tin, and the committee should say openly that they are precursors, not co-discoverers.
statement.case_against: The 2010 overlap remains the strongest objection, and a member who values a new concept over an enabling method can reasonably prefer B014. Precursor credit for Kosugi and Migita, and the contemporaneous Guram and Rennels work, rests partly on my recollection of the history and is not fully settled by the files. B014 has a genuinely new pharmacological principle, a larger pipeline and three first-place openings, which B046 cannot match on novelty. The chair's observation fairly states the trade-off: B014 leads on novelty with an open credit question, and B046 leads on credit with an open novelty question.

responses.point: Aili argues that PROTACs and cereblon glues form one principle of induced proximity to an E3 ligase, and that late-stage trials make approval unnecessary for the science to count as durable.
responses.response: Her unifying argument is the strongest case for B014 I have seen, and it moved me to list B014 as my first alternative. I still see a problem in the evidence: the cereblon mechanism was found after the clinical drugs worked, while the PROTAC concept was a designed one, so the two strands have different logic and different people. Crediting Handa without Ito, who shared the cereblon paper, adds an attribution difficulty beyond the three-name cap. Durability of the science is not in dispute, but the committee is also weighing credit, and B046 has none of this ambiguity, so I do not change my ranking.

responses.point: Aqvist would resist splitting B014 into two parts because it would exceed the cap, and says one citation around induced degradation covers both lines.
responses.response: I agree that a split is not available, since two parts with Crews, Deshaies, Handa and Ciulli would exceed three people. That leaves the one-citation route, and I doubt a citation can be both accurate and short when the lines include a designed concept and a mechanism discovered after the fact. His own file names Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim as serious claims left out, which is the weakness I rely on. I note his fallback is B027; I would find that cleaner than B014 on credit, though I rank it below B046 for the reasons I gave Linke.

responses.point: Sparr now prefers B060 with Cullis, Hope and Madden, calling the Vancouver trio the cleanest attribution chain and arguing that pKa-dependent charge and non-bilayer phase behaviour are physical-chemical principles.
responses.response: The pKa-controlled charge and endosomal-escape logic is real chemistry, and I accept her correction that my sixth ranking understated it. My remaining difficulty is credit, not science: she lists Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan as decisive for later products, and she raises patent disputes and the overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize herself. With six credited names and a three-name cap, any cut will be contested, whereas B046 needs no cut. I also grant that the molecular definition of a lipid formulation is looser than a catalytic cycle.

responses.point: Somfai disagrees with my base-editing ranking and holds that B053 is a protein-engineering fusion built on CRISPR (2020) with early clinical evidence and unresolved credit for Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo.
responses.response: That is persuasive and I change on it: I no longer treat B053 as a leading alternative and have replaced it with B014. I think he is right that a Liu-only prize would leave a fairness question over the trainees and the parallel Nishida and Kondo work, and that the CRISPR overlap weakens novelty. His request to check the Migita, Guram and Rennels history before fixing the citation is also right, and I would accept wording that says catalytic C-N cross-coupling and states Kosugi's work as precedent.

responses.point: Linke prefers B027, noting unambiguous two-author credit and four decades of use, and asks whether B046 can be told apart from the 2010 prize.
responses.response: I accept that B027 has the same credit clarity as B046 and a long record, and I hold no objection on maturity. My gap with him is how widely a first-principles dynamics method shapes chemical practice compared with a reaction run in synthesis laboratories every day, and the shadow of the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes weighs more there than the 2010 shadow weighs on B046. His question on the 2010 prize is answered above: this is a different bond-forming step with its own ligand logic. I would not rank B027 above B046 but I would not oppose it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the C-N versus C-C distinction as sufficient novelty beyond the 2010 prize.
Precursor history for Kosugi, Migita, Guram and Rennels, which I recall from memory and have not verified from the provided files.
Whether the unifying induced-proximity argument for B014 can yield a defensible three-name cut, and whether the absence of an approved PROTAC will matter to other members.
What the other members would accept if B046 and B014 each fall short of five votes.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with Buchwald, Hartwig or any other credited name on the shortlist; no change from round 1. My field of electron crystallography and porous materials is not represented on this shortlist. I know Secretary Brzezinski only as a Stockholm University colleague, and no shortlisted candidate is linked to either of us.
